problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

The quadrilateral $Q$ is mapped to the quadrilateral ${Q}^{′}$ under the action of $T.$ The quadrilateral ${Q}^{′}$ has vertices $(0,4),(-4,4),(12,4),$ and $(7,3).$ Which of the following are vertices of $Q?$

- $(-2,4)$
- $(1,-2)$
- $(4,4)$
worked_solution:
First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of ${Q}^{′}:$ 

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of $Q$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2-0}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 12 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -8 & 8 & 4 \\ 8 & 8 & 8 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 4 & 2 \\ 4 & 4 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the coordinates of $Q$ are $(-2,4),(-4,4),(4,4),(2,3).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
